Supporting_Result: Frozen nominal and measured definitions were applied to the same retained physical capacity records.
Important_Limitation: The analysis does not establish a universally correct reference.
Recommended_Wording: Qref should be treated as an explicit benchmark-definition choice.

Supporting_Result: SOH was defined as Q/Qref, and cell-level Qref deviations had opposite directions across datasets.
Important_Limitation: The transformation changes labels, not physical degradation.
Recommended_Wording: Changing Qref rescaled SOH labels for an unchanged capacity observation.

Discussion_Point: Qref shifts the analytical EOL threshold
Supporting_Result: The absolute threshold was alpha multiplied by Qref at 75%, 80%, and 85%.
Important_Limitation: The direction follows algebraically from Qref ordering.
Recommended_Wording: Under the predefined labeling rule, Qref shifted the absolute EOL threshold.

Supporting_Result: At 80%, status changed in 51/55 and 49/55 XJTU cells and in 77/77 HUST cells for the two measured definitions.
Important_Limitation: Counts depend on observation density and released windows.
Recommended_Wording: Qref definition changed the observed EOL censoring state within the frozen observation windows.

Discussion_Point: Qref can determine whether point-RUL exists
Supporting_Result: At 80%, point-RUL availability changed from 20/55 to 0/55 in XJTU and from 0/77 to 77/77 in HUST.
Important_Limitation: This concerns point-label availability, not true remaining life.
Recommended_Wording: Qref definition changed whether a point-RUL label was available under the censoring rules.

Discussion_Point: SOH-space errors can exaggerate label-scale differences
Supporting_Result: SOH-space errors changed with Qref scaling while physical-space MAE_Q remained directly comparable in Ah.
Important_Limitation: The pattern is descriptive and not identical for every model-dataset pair.
Recommended_Wording: SOH-space errors were generally more sensitive to label scaling than physical-capacity-space errors.

Discussion_Point: Physical-capacity-space evaluation reduces pure scaling ambiguity
Supporting_Result: The primary ranking metric used median cell MAE_Q_Ah rather than an SOH-normalized error.
Important_Limitation: Physical-space metrics do not remove protocol, feature, or model effects.
Recommended_Wording: Reporting MAE_Q alongside SOH-space errors reduced ambiguity due solely to Qref scaling.

Discussion_Point: Model ranking was stable in the primary analysis
Supporting_Result: Random Forest ranked first, Gradient Boosting second, and Ridge third for all six dataset-by-common-Qref combinations.
Important_Limitation: This ranking is specific to the frozen models, folds, features, and metric.
Recommended_Wording: Primary model rank positions were stable under the predefined median cell MAE_Q metric.

Discussion_Point: One A8 descriptive reversal was not bootstrap robust
Supporting_Result: RF and GB exchanged observed rank positions for measured Qrefs, but all corrected difference-of-medians 95% CIs included zero.
Important_Limitation: Observed-sample bootstrap stability is not a universal superiority probability.
Recommended_Wording: The XJTU A8 RF/GB reversal was descriptive and not bootstrap robust.

Discussion_Point: Threshold effects were not unique to 80%
Supporting_Result: Frozen 75%, 80%, and 85% analyses all contained Qref-related label effects, with threshold-specific observability.
Important_Limitation: The magnitude and estimability changed with threshold and observation window.
Recommended_Wording: Qref-related labeling effects occurred across all three predefined thresholds.

Supporting_Result: XJTU sparse diagnostics produced interval/right censoring; HUST 75% and nominal 80% were constrained by the finite released window and stopping-rule context.
Important_Limitation: Censoring states do not identify unobserved physical event times.
Recommended_Wording: EOL and point-RUL results should be interpreted conditional on observation density and stopping rules.
